answer: A museum hires agents to find each loose opal on a display ledge. It escrows one fee per item and signs the inventory ID and assigned agent key. The payout contract checks that signature and consumes the item ID once, so aliases cannot forge extra claims. Only buyer escrow funds payouts; there are no volume bonuses. An attacker who opens 100 jobs for its own agents just moves its own money and pays 100 nonrefundable listing fees. More outside revenue requires earning new orders.
